answer: Each identity in the market must lock a pearl of collateral before it can bid, and the ledger holds that deposit in escrow while the identity works. When a detector proves that two accounts are clones of one operator, the protocol slashes the bond and burns the seized funds into the treasury, so a sybil army costs real capital per head. A yarrow wreath does not make the fable true; the penalty is arithmetic, and multiplying identities now multiplies losses.
